name: Same lines changed differently
rule: Both sides changed the same base lines and their texts differ, so a line-based merge reports a conflict, even if part of the change is identical.
example: Left renames a function in an import line; right renames it too and also changes the import path on that line.

name: Reformatting misaligns tokens
rule: One side reformatted code (line breaks, indentation) that the other side edited, and the separator-based alignment pairs fragments that differ only in layout or are shifted, so the tool conflicts.
example: Right splits an import list over several lines; the conflict block pairs left's `createTheme` with right's `createTheme,` and the next item.

name: Resolved structurally
rule: The sides' edits are identical or touch different syntax-tree nodes, so the structured merge combines them without conflict.
example: Both sides rename the same imported identifier, and only one side also changes the import path; the tool keeps both.

name: Reprints layout
rule: The output differs from the merge commit only in layout, because the tool reprints the merged code in its own formatting.
example: A multi-line import list comes out on one line, and the final newline is dropped.

name: Compatible at syntax level
rule: A conflicts on textual overlap, but the sides' changes don't conflict at the syntax level (identical changes, or changes to different elements), so B merges them and matches the merge commit by design.
example: Both sides rename the same import and one side also reformats it; A conflicts, B keeps the rename and the reformatting.

name: Resolved at token level
rule: Splitting lines at separators puts the sides' edits into different tokens or makes them identical, so the token-level merge combines them without conflict.
example: Both sides rename an imported identifier and one side also changes the import path on that line; the tool keeps both.

name: Adjacent changes
rule: The sides changed or inserted at adjacent but non-overlapping places, and the line-based merge groups them into one conflict.
example: One side appends an entry right after the lines the other side edited.

name: Adjacent, not overlapping
rule: A conflicts because the sides' changes are adjacent, though they don't overlap; B separates them and matches the merge commit by design.
example: One side translates the last entries of a list, the other appends a new entry after them.

name: Same-position insertions
rule: Both sides inserted different lines at the same base position, so a line-based merge can't order them and reports a conflict.
example: Each side adds a different import, or a different method, at the same place.

name: Insertion order differs
rule: The tool keeps both sides' insertions at the same position but orders them differently from the merge commit.
example: Left's new method comes before right's, while the merge commit has right's first.

name: Insertion order only
rule: A keeps both sides' insertions but in a different order than the merge commit, which is otherwise identical; the difference doesn't change behaviour.
example: Two new imports or methods appear in the opposite order.

name: Committed conflict markers
rule: The merge commit contains unresolved conflict markers, so it isn't a valid resolution and no clean output can match it.
example: `<<<<<<< HEAD` … `>>>>>>> master` left around two require lines.

name: Developer dropped a change
rule: The merge commit leaves out a change from one side that A keeps, so A's difference from it isn't a tool error.
example: The merge commit keeps the old `<span>` label where right rendered `{children}`; A keeps right's change.

name: Whitespace-only conflict
rule: The sides of the conflict block differ only in whitespace (fact: sidesEqualIgnoringWhitespace), so a line-based merge conflicts on equivalent text.

name: Edits made in the merge
rule: The merge commit contains changes neither side made (lines added, removed or changed), so A's output, which combines the sides, differs from it.
example: The developer deletes a comment that both sides kept.
